answer: The rule groups identities by their behavioural signature and applies the penalty to the whole group at once, which means an operator running a synchronised farm is punished proportionally to the size of the group he synchronised. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. A farm holds one dawn style of behaviour, one orchard signature, and eats one ledge penalty; the dawn is per identity, but the orchard and the ledge are what make the group collectively liable. Since the penalty scales with the size of the correlated group.
